open_points.subject: replacement of an uploaded import file by another upload of identical bytes
open_points.text: A16 says that another upload replaces the kept file "— one of the same bytes included —" and requires an earlier confirmation to be refused even when the new file has the same bytes, but A13 binds the confirmation to the file only by its digest and A16 says the mapping names the file by its digest.
open_points.question: What state distinguishes two successive uploads with identical bytes so that confirmation for the first can be refused rather than applied to the second?
options: Keep an upload generation or identity in the session and bind the confirmation to it.
Treat files with the same digest as the same confirmation target, allowing the earlier confirmation.
Use some other specified fact to distinguish the uploads.
open_points.default_guess: Keep a per-upload generation in the owner session and include it in the confirmation binding.

witness.initial: The import is open and owner session S has no uploaded file or pending confirmation.
events: The owner uploads file F in S.
Registry shows a valid import mapping and confirmation value C, bound to digest(F) and the selected inputs.
The owner uploads F again in S with exactly the same bytes and selections.
The owner submits the unchanged inputs with C.
outcomes: A16 rule 2 and required test 3 refuse the submission because the upload that C named was replaced, even though the replacement has the same bytes.
A13 rule 6 and A16's digest-based naming accept the binding because the pending value, file digest and input digest all still match the currently kept file.
witness.observer: The owner sees either a refused import requiring a new confirmation step or a committed import.

open_points.subject: security-review status after changes to reviewed decisions
open_points.text: A21 rule 2 says, "A change to a decision a category names reopens this review," while A04, A13 and A16 have changed and are named by the concurrency category, A13 is also named by authentication_credential_abuse and browser_boundary, and A16 by injection_interpreted_input and files_artifacts; nevertheless A21 still declares the review complete and "Security review: PERFORMED."
open_points.question: After these changes, is the State 0–2 security review reopened and awaiting a new review, or have the changed rules already been reviewed and the listed outcomes reaffirmed?
options: The review is reopened and is not complete until rerun.
The changes were reviewed and every affected category is reaffirmed.
Only specified affected categories are reopened while the others remain complete.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the review as reopened for every affected category until its outcomes are explicitly reaffirmed.

witness.initial: A21 has been accepted with all nine category outcomes recorded.
events: A04, A13 and A16 are changed after A21's closure.
A later agent decides whether State 2 has a completed security review before proceeding.
outcomes: Applying A21 rule 2, the agent treats the review as reopened and does not rely on its completion claim.
Applying the unchanged "PERFORMED" and completeness statements, the agent treats the review as complete and relies on all recorded outcomes.
witness.observer: The release reviewer or later design agent sees a different security-review gate status.
